Everything looks good which means we can proceed to modelling. First we have to generate Presence-Absence data. To do so, we are going to nee
to make some assumptions about the parameters.

We will draw values $Y$ from the prior predictive distirbution $p(Y|D, \theta)$. To generate from the ppd, we can do a variety of things. We can either fit a SO model
to the data and use these estimates to generate the PA data. Or we can fit the Presence-only model, and sample from the posterior of this, for each repetition of the PA data. 

```{r data-setup}
# Prepare data for feeding into stan models
link <- "cloglog"
data_reps <- 20
covar_df <- st_drop_geometry(subgrid_covars)
colnames(covar_df)
#intensity_covars <- covar_df[c("evi", "elev", "frac_111", )]
intensity_covars <- covar_df[c("evi", "elev", "frac_111", "frac_115", "frac_124")]
bias_covars <- covar_df[c("frac_50")]#"duration_minutes", "number_observers",  "effort_distance_km", "time_observations_started", 
k_param_intn <- length(colnames(intensity_covars)) 
k_param_bias <- length(colnames(bias_covars)) 
dim(as.matrix(covar_df))
p_detection <- 0.2
n_surveys <- 5
sites <- nrow(covar_df)
sites
sum(covar_df$counts)
```

```{r fit-ppd}
model_path <- "nuthatch_poisson_process.stan"
model_string <- nuthatch_poisson_process
write(model_string, model_path)
data_site_occ = list(N=sites, X=intensity_covars, y=covar_df$counts, Z=bias_covars, k_i=k_param_intn, k_b=k_param_bias)
model <- cmdstan_model(model_path) 
fit <- model$sample(data=data_site_occ, seed=13, chains=3, iter_sampling=2000, iter_warmup=500) 
```

```{r PA-data}
# Extract the posterior draws from the stan fit
pp_posterior <- fit$draws(intensity_params, format="matrix")
colnames(pp_posterior)
dim(pp_posterior)
# Get 1000 samples from the posterior
p_index <- sample(c(1:1000), size = 1000, replace = T)
pp_posterior <- pp_posterior[p_index, ]
dim(pp_posterior)

generate_ebird_pa <- function(data_reps, surface_data, p_0, pp_posterior, n, sites, link){
  # Generate some random covariate data that will be used to model theta
  # Add a column of 1s to the auxiliary data
  a_intercept <- rep(1, nrow(surface_data))
  surface_data <- cbind(a_intercept, surface_data)
  occupancy_maps <- matrix(nrow=data_reps, ncol=sites)
  Y_detection <- matrix(nrow=data_reps, ncol=sites)
  theta_reps <- matrix(nrow=data_reps, ncol=sites)
  for (r in 1:data_reps){
    # Equivalent way to induce correlation
    #R <- t(chol(corr_matrix)) 
    #theta <- b_0 + sampling_surface$aux*b_1 + R %*% rnorm(sites)
    param_vec <- pp_posterior[r,]
    if (link=="cloglog"){
      g_theta <- 1 - exp(-exp(as.matrix(surface_data)%*%t(param_vec)))
    }
    stopifnot(sites==length(g_theta))
    site_presence <- rbinom(sites, 1, g_theta)
    theta_reps[r, ] <- g_theta
    occupancy_maps[r, ] <- site_presence
    Y_detection[r, ] <- rbinom(sites, n, p_0*site_presence)
  } 
  return(list(occupancy=occupancy_maps, Y=Y_detection, theta=theta_reps))
}

# Generate the data by drawing over the posterior of the parameters
pa_gen <- generate_ebird_pa(data_reps, intensity_covars, p_detection, pp_posterior, n_surveys, sites, link)

# Create plots of the occupancy and probability maps
for(d_i in 1:20){
  occ_map <- st_geometry(subgrid_covars) %>% st_sf()
  occ_map$occ <- pa_gen$occupancy[d_i,]
  occ_map$prob <- pa_gen$theta[d_i,]
  occ_map$counts <- pa_gen$Y[d_i,]
  
  # Then plot the predictions
  occ_rast <- terra::rasterize(vect(occ_map), crop_evi_rast, field="occ")
  p <- ggplot() + 
      geom_spatraster(data=occ_rast) +
      scale_fill_viridis_c(begin=0.2, end=1, option="viridis",alpha=0.8, na.value="white") +
      #geom_sf(data = prj_state, color=alpha("black",0.4), fill='transparent', linewidth=0.7) + 
      theme_minimal()+
      ggtitle("Occupancy maps generated over Prior Predictive Distribtion")
  print(p)
  
  prob_rast <- terra::rasterize(vect(occ_map), crop_evi_rast, field="prob")
  p <- ggplot() + 
      geom_spatraster(data=prob_rast) +
      scale_fill_viridis_c(begin=0.2, end=1, option="viridis",alpha=0.8, na.value="white") +
      #geom_sf(data = prj_state, color=alpha("black",0.4), fill='transparent', linewidth=0.7) + 
      theme_minimal()+
      ggtitle("Probability maps generated over Prior Predictive Distribtion")
  print(p)
  
  count_rast <- terra::rasterize(vect(occ_map), crop_evi_rast, field="counts")
  p <- ggplot() + 
      geom_spatraster(data=count_rast) +
      scale_fill_viridis_c(begin=0.2, end=1, option="viridis",alpha=0.8, na.value="white") +
      #geom_sf(data = prj_state, color=alpha("black",0.4), fill='transparent', linewidth=0.7) + 
      theme_minimal()+
      ggtitle("Counts at sites generated over Prior Predictive Distribtion")
  print(p)
}
```

Check out some other resources about occupancy modelling in stan: UBMS, Richard erickson "occupancy modelling in stan"

Using the PO data and generated PA data, we can now fit our site-occupancy model. We randomly sample $m$ sites for the PA likelihood.
```{r model-fit}
# We will use the same data as we used to fit the PO model, only now we will also randomly sample a select set of 
# sites to use as PA data in the SO model. Otherwise the set-up stays the same.
m <- 20
#site_idx <- sample(which(pa_gen$Y[10,]>0), m, replace=F)
site_idx <- sample(1:sites, m, replace=F)
site_idx
covars_sampled_sites <- intensity_covars[site_idx, ]
dim(covars_sampled_sites)
covars_sampled_sites
# The PA counts are those generated from the PP parameters above.
# For the sake of illustration we pick 1 dataset
selected_counts <- pa_gen$Y[10,site_idx]
selected_counts
n_surveys <- rep(n_surveys, m)
data_site_occ = list(n_surveys=n_surveys, n_pa_sites=m, n_po_sites=sites, X=covars_sampled_sites, Y=selected_counts, PO=covar_df$counts,
                         X_po=intensity_covars, Z_po=bias_covars, k_i=k_param_intn, k_b=k_param_bias, model_diag=0)
model_path <- "nuthatch_site_occ.stan"
model_string <- nuthatch_poisson_process_site_occupancy
write(model_string, model_path)
model <- cmdstan_model(model_path) 
fit <- model$sample(data=data_site_occ, seed=13, chains=3, iter_sampling=2000, iter_warmup=500) 
```

```{r model-inspect}
occ_mode_rast <- terra::rasterize(vect(subgrid_geo), crop_evi_rast, field="occ_mode")
p <- ggplot() + 
    geom_spatraster(data=occ_mode_rast) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(begin=0.2, end=1, option="viridis",alpha=0.8, na.value="white") +
    #geom_sf(data = prj_state, color=alpha("black",0.4), fill='transparent', linewidth=0.7) + 
    theme_minimal()+
    ggtitle("Predicted occupancy mode at nuthatch sites")
print(p)
# Oops if we have probability less than 0.5 mode is always 0.
prob_pred_rast <- terra::rasterize(vect(subgrid_geo), crop_evi_rast, field="prob_pred")
p <- ggplot() + 
    geom_spatraster(data=prob_pred_rast) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(begin=0.2, end=1, option="viridis",alpha=0.8, na.value="white") +
    #geom_sf(data = prj_state, color=alpha("black",0.4), fill='transparent', linewidth=0.7) + 
    theme_minimal()+
    ggtitle("Generated occupancy probability at nuthatch sites")
print(p)
```
That summarizes the work needed to generate PA data using the prior predictive distribution from a PP when we have real data.
